questions.questionText: What problem does k-fold cross-validation solve compared to a single train/test split?
options: It removes the dependency on which specific examples happened to land in the test set, by testing on every example exactly once
It eliminates the need for a test set entirely, forever
It automatically picks the best model architecture
questions.correctAnswer: It removes the dependency on which specific examples happened to land in the test set, by testing on every example exactly once
questions.explanation: A single split can be lucky or unlucky; averaging performance across k folds, where every example is tested on exactly once, gives a more reliable estimate.

questions.questionText: What's wrong with tuning a hyperparameter by repeatedly checking performance on your final test set?
options: Nothing is wrong with this approach
It effectively overfits to the test set itself, since you keep selecting whatever choice happens to score best on it
It only works for classification, not regression
questions.correctAnswer: It effectively overfits to the test set itself, since you keep selecting whatever choice happens to score best on it
questions.explanation: Repeatedly peeking at test performance to make decisions turns the test set into a de facto training signal, defeating its purpose as an unbiased final check.

questions.questionText: In 5-fold cross-validation, how many times is each individual example used for training?
questions.explanation: Each example is held out for testing in exactly 1 of the 5 folds, and used for training in the other 4.
